title: Bowdoin vs ConnCollege: tuition, size, location
summary: Bowdoin College (Bowdoin) versus Connecticut College (ConnCollege). Also searched as ConnCollege vs Bowdoin. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Connecticut College and Bowdoin College are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes in the College Scorecard. Connecticut College, located in New London, has an undergraduate enrollment of 1,937 students, slightly higher than Bowdoin College's 1,873 students in Brunswick. Tuition costs are comparable, with Connecticut College charging $67,242 and Bowdoin College $67,832 for in-state students. These similarities highlight their shared status as private liberal arts colleges, while their geographic locations distinguish them.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Connecticut College and Bowdoin College have similar tuition rates for both in-state and out-of-state students, with Connecticut College charging $67,242 and Bowdoin College $67,832. Despite these close tuition costs, the median debt for students who complete their degrees differs, with Connecticut College graduates carrying a median debt of $23,500 compared to Bowdoin College graduates who have a median debt of $18,500. This difference in median debt may reflect variations in financial aid packages or student borrowing patterns between the two institutions.

When comparing Connecticut College versus Bowdoin College, the tuition fees are nearly identical, but the disparity in median debt suggests that students at Bowdoin may graduate with less financial burden. Both colleges maintain high tuition costs typical of private liberal arts schools, but the financial outcomes for students can vary, as seen in these debt figures.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Connecticut College and Bowdoin College both employ a traditional liberal arts learning model, emphasizing a broad-based undergraduate education. Connecticut College, situated in New London, Connecticut, enrolls 1,937 undergraduate students, while Bowdoin College, located in Brunswick, Maine, has a slightly smaller undergraduate population of 1,873. Both campuses provide residential experiences that support close faculty-student interaction and a community-oriented environment. The geographic settings of New London and Brunswick contribute to distinct campus cultures, with Connecticut College positioned in a coastal city in the northeastern United States and Bowdoin College located in a smaller Maine town. These factors influence the overall student experience alongside their shared commitment to liberal arts education.
